title: Pesto Tomato Chicken Tray
seoTitle: Pesto Tomato Chicken Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Basil pesto chicken with roasted cherry tomatoes and zucchini
subtitle: Basil pesto chicken with roasted cherry tomatoes and zucchini
description: Chicken thighs roast with cherry tomatoes and zucchini, brushed with basil pesto until golden and fragrant.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Pesto Tomato Chicken Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss tomatoes and zucchini with olive oil, salt, and pepper on two half-sheets until lightly coated. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season chicken
steps.instruction: Pat thighs dry, season with salt and pepper. Nest skin-side up among vegetables with space between pieces for air circulation. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Initial roast
steps.instruction: Roast 18 minutes until chicken skin renders fat and turns lightly golden while tomatoes begin to soften at edges. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Brush with pesto
steps.instruction: Brush pesto over chicken and vegetables. Sprinkle parmesan. Roast 10–12 more minutes until chicken hits 165°F and pesto edges caramelize. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.instruction: Top with fresh basil. Tomatoes should burst with juice; zucchini tender with slight bite at center. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Thin pesto with 1 tbsp olive oil if too thick to brush evenly.
Serve over polenta or pasta for a fuller plate.
Sun-dried tomato pesto swap works if basil pesto is unavailable.
tonightSpread: Creamy polenta in a hotel pan.
leftovers: Slice chicken into pesto pasta next day.
Chop into a wrap with extra pesto and mozzarella.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Summer flavors year-round. One tray, minimal cleanup, and the kitchen smells incredible.
mealPrepNotes: Use store pesto or make a batch ahead. Zucchini adds moisture—do not skip. Station: Brush pesto last 12 minutes—early application burns basil. Station: Cut zucchini thick so it roasts, not steams, under chicken. Station: Finish with fresh basil at the line for bright color.
